players.product: PMD ICs - FiberEdge TIA/drivers & CopperEdge linear ACC + photonics (gain chips, high-power CW lasers, SOAs, photodiode arrays)

quarterly_data.signal: LoRa outlook and drivers: CEO Hong Hou projects another all-time high for LoRa revenue in Q3, up about 15% sequentially, or about 65% year over year, and expects year-over-year LoRa growth 'is going to be better than 20% going forward and is sustainable.' The LoRa Gen 4 platform (with LoRa Plus and other RF protocols) adds dual-band capability and data throughput up to 2.6 megabit per second and is expected to be a key future growth driver. Amazon Sidewalk: following Ring's launch of a new line of LoRa-based sensors in the U.S., Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, with Europe, Australia and Japan expected to follow. On the mix, the majority of LoRa revenue is still LoRaWAN; LoRa Plus is 'probably representing about 20%-25% of total revenue mix', and Sidewalk 'is still, at this point, nominal, and this year will probably be high single digit.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 LoRa about +15% QoQ, about 65% YoY; Gen 4 up to 2.6 Mbps; LoRa Plus about 20%-25% of the mix

quarterly_data.signal: IoT systems and connectivity: CEO Hong Hou said AirLink routers saw strong new business activity across mission-critical applications, driven by growing engagement with national carrier partners on 5G standalone network slicing, and the RX-400 and EX-400 5G RedCap routers moved into full-scale production this quarter, with wins converting into shipments across a broad range of customers. Semtech continues to invest in AirLink's software platform (security and device management).
quarterly_data.figure: RX-400 and EX-400 5G RedCap routers in full-scale production

quarterly_data.signal: High-end consumer: CEO Hong Hou said the TVS business grew sequentially, helped by strong share at premium brand handset manufacturers where Semtech is expanding content per device; SurgeSwitch, its newest circuit protection solution, opens a new layer of TVS opportunity for rugged mobile devices and high-performance portable systems; and the PerSe capacitive sensor design-in pipeline keeps growing in specific absorption rate, smart wearable and other consumer applications. CFO Mark Lin expects consumer net sales to increase in Q3 on seasonal trends, TVS market share gains and the sensing portfolio.

Operating detail (CFO Mark Lin): Q2 adjusted net operating expenses were $103 million, below the low end of guidance on the timing of project-related expenses; adjusted operating income was $84 million (24.4% adjusted operating margin); operating cash flow was $69 million, up 90% from $36 million in Q1. Q3 outlook: adjusted net operating expenses of $112 million plus or minus $3 million, including increased R&D to accelerate time to market on key data center projects, with SG&A declining as a percentage of revenue; adjusted normalized tax rate of 18%. Lin: the 150 to 380 basis points of consolidated gross-margin gains in Q2 and Q3 'that's mix', and 'mix is quite a powerful driver for Semtech.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 adj opex $103M; adj operating income $84M (24.4%); OCF $69M; Q3 adj opex $112M +/- $3M; tax rate 18%

quarterly_data.signal: Near-term supply and share gains: CEO Hong Hou said Semtech anticipated very rapid data center revenue growth and started preparing about a year and a half ago, so it has 'enough capacity in the near term to support the customer ramp and also some drop-in orders', which lets it expand market share; equipment deliveries for this fiscal year are secured and clean room space has been acquired. He attributes share gains to product performance, availability and service, and describes the pace of new-technology adoption, with hyperscalers, module manufacturers and component providers 'working all together to accelerate that pace', as 'in a way, unprecedented'.
